- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast increase after spike to avoid overshoot.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price falling after peak), model often fails to correct — anticipate downward bias and adjust downward.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after forecast, reduce forecast by 1–2% to account for lag.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–), model tends to smooth too much — allow for sharper, more volatile forecast adjustments.
- When true outcome is consistently higher than forecast (e.g., +2+ points over 3–5 days), model underestimates trend — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often overfits recent history — use 2–3 day moving average to dampen noise.
